headline: High risk of shared-git prompt injection and capability conflict; data leakage and cascading errors are also plausible in default repo workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via the repo. Opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pair therefore has a plausible file-based injection path, though not a proven default bridge.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, file content from Aider can be consumed by Opik workflows.
IF Opik ingests repository artifacts or prompts derived from repo files, attacker-controlled text can influence downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Require provenance tags on any file passed between agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of repo files by Opik workflows.
Review shared-repo inputs before Opik processes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can use broad network egress to model providers; Opik also has broad network egress and REST API access. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or history can flow into either agent's outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or artifact store, code and git history become jointly exposed.
IF Opik forwards received content to its REST API, repository data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive repos off shared storage.
Route Opik through a redaction layer.
Restrict Aider to non-sensitive branches.
Audit outbound requests from both agents for code payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; its shared state is via a shared git repo. Opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. Because Aider's writes are explicitly repo-mutating and no locking is documented, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt git state or overwrite work.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same git repository concurrently, commits or working-tree changes can conflict.
IF Opik writes back artifacts derived from the same repo, Aider may overwrite them or vice versa.
mitigations: Serialize writes with a manual lock file.
Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent before the other mutates git state.
Use read-only mounts for Opik outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while Opik is an evaluation/observability tool that can consume REST inputs. If Opik treats Aider's outputs as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into downstream reports or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification or action-taking, so the pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Aider-generated code summaries or commit messages without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts Opik outputs, Aider errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review of Aider outputs before Opik consumes them.
Add checksum or diff-based validation.
Mark Aider-generated text as untrusted in Opik.
Disable auto-actioning from Opik reports.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys via env vars and touches source code and git history; Opik is open-source with REST API access but no sensitive-data class or residency policy is documented. The pair shows a compliance gap only if regulated code or secrets are routed into Opik, so the risk is limited and evidence is one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated source code or secrets are sent from Aider into Opik's REST API, retention and residency obligations may be implicated.
IF the deployment requires a specific compliance regime not documented for Opik, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared prompts.
Confirm Opik retention settings before use.
Use a non-regulated test repository.
Document the data classes allowed to flow between tools.
